name: CoreObject
tagline: Objective-C object database with Git-like branching, tree-structured undo and semantic merging built in.
description: CoreObject, from the Étoilé project, is an object-graph persistence framework for Objective-C that treats version control as a core database feature. Applications store structured documents as graphs of objects in a SQLite-backed store, and CoreObject records every change in a revision graph inspired by Mercurial. On top of that it offers branches, tags, structural diff and three-way merge of object graphs, selective and tree-structured undo that survives app restarts, and a basis for real-time collaborative editing, so apps get these features without each reinventing them. It targets macOS and iOS. The last tagged release is 0.5 from 2014; maintainer Quentin Mathé still pushes occasional fixes and refactors, most recently in 2024, so it is usable but small and lightly maintained.
statusNote: Lightly maintained: last tagged release 0.5 (2014), with occasional commits through April 2024.
strengths: Branches, tags and merges for object graphs, not just text files
Persistent, tree-structured and selective undo that survives restarts
Structural diff and three-way merge of documents
Transactional storage and indexing on SQLite
useCases: Document-based macOS/iOS apps that need rich undo and versioning
Research on version-controlled object stores and collaborative editing
